text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today as oil prices dropped over 2% on concerns that elevated crude costs could dampen fuel demand. The broader weakness reflects traders reassessing the balance between supply risks (Saudi infrastructure attacks, Middle East tensions) and demand destruction — the risk that high oil prices force consumers and businesses to cut back on fuel consumption. This matters for a refiner like Marathon because while higher crude prices can boost profits under some conditions, demand destruction erodes the volume of fuel they can sell at those prices.

The stock has retreated nearly 5% in six days despite refineries running at 93.4% capacity and oil storage remaining relatively low — suggesting the market is pricing in a meaningful slowdown in fuel demand rather than viewing the geopolitical premium in crude as a pure tailwind for refining margins.
